To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) efficient electron transport in small molecules is possible due to the intermolecular charge transfer, (ii) this charge delocalization can be multidimensional, (iii) the delocalization is more efficient in the case of the F2 molecule than the TCNQ molecule, and this is the main reason for the higher mobility in F2-TCND compared to TCNQ.
the charge delocalization dimensionality and not the size of the molecule is important for the charge transport mechanism, which is in contradiction to the common understanding.

the intermolecular charge transport mechanism is band-like in F2-TCNO crystals and that the intermolecule charge delocalization, rather than the intramolecular reorganization energy, is the main reason for the high electron mobility in this material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of intermolecular electronic delocalization in efficient band-like charge transport in organic materials.
the role of intermolecular delocalization in the charge transport in organic molecular crystals.
the theoretical understanding of charge transport mechanisms in crystalline materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the high electron mobility of F2-TCNDQ is due to the intermolecular delocalization of the electron wave function in three directions, and this is a result of the interplay of the molecular structure, the crystal packing, and the electron-electron repulsion.
the charge transport is band-like, and the electron mobility in F2-TCND crystals can be as high as 10 cm(2) V-1 s(-1) at room temperature.

the charge transport in F2-TCQN is band-like and efficient, but the charge transport in TCNQ is hopping-like and inefficient, due to the absence of multidimensional intermoclecular charge delocalization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intermolecular charge transfer in F2-TCQ crystal is not a simple two-dimensional process but rather a complex three-dimensional process.
the intermolecular charge-delocalization dimensionality is a crucial parameter that should be included in the search for high-performance organic semiconducting materials.
the charge transport in organic crystals is not a simple hopping mechanism but is rather band-like with a strong interplay between intermolecular charge transfer and intramolecular reorganization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intermolecular charge transfer (IMCT) mechanism is not necessarily a sign of an inefficient charge transport.
a high electron mobility is not a unique property of the F2-TNCQ molecule, but can be obtained by a careful molecular design.
a small reorganization energy does not necessarily imply efficient charge transport.
